```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is stronger and better sourced in B. Competitors publish prices of $29.99–$124/month (EstimationPro $66/$124, Outdoor Estimates $49.99, QuoteIQ from $29.99). A business buyer is paying to save billable time. In A, buyers pay $4–7/month, and A's own demand quote says users want it 'free to use' because caregivers are 'financially stressed.'",
    "For a single paying customer within 90 days, B's buyer decides alone. A's product depends on multi-sibling adoption, which its own brief calls documented activation friction.",
    "B's pain is quantified by the user: '1-2 hours' every evening writing quotes. That gives a concrete time-saved value to sell against. A's pain evidence is real but describes workarounds (Google Sheets, group texts) that cost users nothing.",
    "B's regulatory burden is lighter: standard Stripe PCI SAQ-A scope plus a template privacy policy. A may fall under the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule and Washington's My Health My Data Act, which carries a private right of action. That is a heavier ongoing load for a one-person company.",
    "Both fields are crowded. B has 7 competitors and A has 6+, so competition does not separate them. In A, several competitors offer generous free tiers, which caps its revenue further. A's organic Reddit channel already favors incumbents unprompted.",
    "B has real weaknesses that do not change the pick. Its acquisition cost figure ($237 blended CPL) is a generic B2B SaaS benchmark, not specific to contractors. Its accuracy and trust risk for AI estimates is unresolved. A faces a lower revenue ceiling per customer and similar acquisition uncertainty."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's first demand quote ('That's why I built [an app]...') comes from a founder promoting a competing app, not from a prospective buyer. It is evidence of supply, not demand. Also unsourced is the Case-for claim that SplitKin, TendTo, and CircleCare are one- or two-person teams, along with the claim that SEO and Facebook groups demonstrably work for incumbents.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B rests on only one sourced demand quote; its second quote's URL was not retrieved, so it counts as missing. Its CPL figure is generic, and prices for CostSnap, Roooster, Setell, and QuotrPro are unpublished. B wins mainly on price per customer, a single decision-maker, and lighter regulation, not on strong demand evidence."
}
```
